Program Overview

The ClickHouse PhD Research Internship Program offers doctoral students the opportunity to pursue ambitious research alongside ClickHouse Labs researchers and engineers working on some of the most interesting challenges in databases, systems, and data infrastructure.

Research interns join ClickHouse Labs for approximately 10-12 weeks to explore meaningful research questions, develop new ideas, and investigate technologies that have the potential to advance both the broader research community and the future of ClickHouse.

The program is intentionally designed around research collaboration. Interns are paired with experienced researchers and have the opportunity to pursue work that aligns with their academic interests, ongoing research, and areas of interest within ClickHouse Labs. In some cases, an internship may build on research, a prototype, or a system the student has already begun exploring at their university.

We believe the strongest research relationships extend beyond a single summer. Interns may continue their work after returning to their university through academic research, open-source contributions, publications, or other forms of collaboration. Where there is a strong mutual fit, an internship may become the beginning of a longer-term relationship between the researcher, ClickHouse Labs, and the broader academic community.

During their internship, researchers will have the opportunity to work closely with ClickHouse Labs, engage with ClickHouse's open-source technology and engineering community, share their findings, and contribute to the intellectual life of the broader research community.

Program length: 10-12 weeks, with flexibility based on academic calendars and research needs

Typical timing: Summer, beginning approximately June 1

Locations: Opportunities available across the US and Europe, subject to role and employment requirements. Remote first.

Research environment: ClickHouse Labs

Internship format: Research-focused, mentor-supported, and shaped around areas of mutual research interest

Compensation: commensurate with experience, a monthly stipend will be paid

Research at ClickHouse Labs

ClickHouse Labs explores ambitious ideas at the intersection of databases, distributed systems, data infrastructure, and the broader systems research community.

We believe some of the most interesting advances in these areas happen through close collaboration between industry and academia. ClickHouse Labs brings together researchers and engineers to explore new ideas, investigate challenging technical problems, and connect academic research with real-world systems at scale.

Research interns are an important part of that community. Interns have the opportunity to bring their own research interests and perspectives into ClickHouse Labs while working alongside researchers and engineers who are deeply engaged with both the practical challenges and open research questions shaping the future of data systems.

Program Goals

- Identify exceptional PhD researchers working in areas directly relevant to ClickHouse.

- Give researchers the opportunity to work on meaningful, open-ended problems with ClickHouse Labs.

- Build long-term relationships with researchers and academic institutions.

- Encourage continued research and open-source contributions after the internship.

- Create opportunities for co-authored papers, thesis advising, or other academic collaboration.

- Increase ClickHouse's visibility within the database and systems research community.

- Publish and share meaningful research outcomes through the ClickHouse website and other appropriate channels.

What Makes the Program Different

This is intentionally not a highly structured engineering internship and should not detailed planning. ****But the high-level problem area and expectations should defined several months before the internship begins. This flexibility is intentional and allows ClickHouse Labs to respond to:

- Emerging research questions

- Current ClickHouse priorities

- New academic research

- Interesting systems or database prototypes

- Work candidates have already completed

- Opportunities to apply new research ideas to ClickHouse

The goal is to identify researchers whose work is already closely aligned with areas ClickHouse cares about and then determine the most valuable research problem to pursue together.

Candidate Profile

We are looking for exceptional PhD students conducting research directly relevant to ClickHouse and the broader database/systems space.

Ideal candidates

- Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science or a closely related field

- Conducting research in areas relevant to ClickHouse

- Demonstrated research excellence

- Strong database systems, distributed systems, hardware, or related technical background

- Has demonstrated ability to independently pursue complex research questions

- Ideally has prior experience with ClickHouse open source but not required**.**

- Has research, prototypes, or publications that could translate into meaningful work with ClickHouse

- Interested in continuing research beyond the internship

- Potential interest in open-source contribution and academic collaboration

Candidate Selection Philosophy

The strongest candidates will be researchers whose work is specifically relevant to what ClickHouse Labs wants to explore.

A candidate who has already:

- Worked with ClickHouse

- Built a relevant database or systems prototype

- Published research in an area relevant to ClickHouse

- Explored a technical problem ClickHouse is interested in

may be significantly more valuable than a candidate with an otherwise impressive academic profile but no meaningful connection to our research areas.

Research Areas & Project Scope

Unlike an engineering internship program, specific projects do not need to be defined when recruiting begins.

Research projects may emerge from:

- A candidate's existing research

- A recent academic paper

- A prototype or system the candidate has developed

- An emerging ClickHouse Labs research priority

- An opportunity to test or extend an existing research concept within ClickHouse

If this is relevant and exciting to you, please apply!

Perks

- Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

- Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

- Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

- Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

- A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

- Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy

Who We Are

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Location:

Santa Clara,CA

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

Applied Materials is the leader in materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every new chip and advanced display in the world. Our expertise in modifying materials at atomic levels and on an industrial scale helps our customers - who make smartphones, supercomputers, virtual reality headsets, autonomous vehicles and more - transform their ideas into reality. Our innovations Make Possible® a Better Future.

Inside our company, we apply the idea of make possible as we work together. We value our people and teams who turn possibilities into reality by advancing our strategy, accomplishing great things and empowering others. We are deeply committed to fostering a Culture of Inclusion where every person knows they belong, feels empowered to bring their whole self to work, and is inspired to grow.

TEAM OVERVIEW

Join our dynamic Supply Chain Analytics team as a Data Scientist Intern! Our mission is to revolutionize efficiency by harnessing the power of machine learning, statistical and simulation modeling, generative AI, and actionable insights.

We are dedicated to transforming process efficiency through deep analysis, cutting-edge visualization, and enhanced UI/UX. Our goal is to elevate decision support systems and measurement capabilities, driving substantial improvements in key business metrics. Be a part of our journey to make a significant impact!

HOW WE WORK

AI has changed how fast a data scientist can move. It has not changed what makes one good.

We look for people who use AI tools aggressively to move faster, and who can still explain every line they ship, defend the assumptions behind a model, and recognize an answer that is fluent but wrong. Strong fundamentals first, AI as a multiplier.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Learn the business: how our supply chain operations run, what the underlying data represents, and where decisions get made.
- Perform exploratory data analysis to identify trends, opportunities, and actionable insights.
- Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, transform, and analyze data from multiple sources.
- Develop statistical and machine learning models to support supply chain decision-making.
- Contribute to GenAI and LLM initiatives, including AI-powered search, automation, and business applications, building reusable components where the work can scale.
- Design and enhance dashboards and reports using Tableau and/or Power BI.
- Partner with stakeholders to understand business challenges, gather requirements, and identify opportunities for improvement.
- Translate business needs into technical requirements and develop scalable analytical solutions.
- Communicate findings and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

TECHNICAL SKILLS

Required foundations

- Working knowledge of databases and data modeling (RDBMS concepts, normalization, primary and foreign keys, indexing).
- Working knowledge of SQL (joins, aggregations, CTEs, window functions).
- Working knowledge of Python for data analysis (Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn).
- Machine learning and statistical fundamentals (supervised and unsupervised methods, train/test methodology, evaluation metrics, distributions, sampling, correlation versus causation).
- Coursework or project experience with a cloud data platform and data at scale (Databricks, Snowflake, or BigQuery; distributed processing and partitioning concepts).
- Data visualization with Tableau and/or Power BI.

Applied and AI skills

- Exposure to data engineering concepts (ETL/ELT, ingestion from multiple sources, pipeline design).
- Exposure to GenAI and LLMs (prompting, retrieval augmented generation, LLM APIs, output evaluation).
- Understanding of version control frameworks such as Git and Bitbucket is a plus.

REQUIREMENTS / EDUCATION

- Currently pursuing a Master's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Analytics, or another quantitative field.
- GPA of 3.0 or above preferred.

IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate learns a new domain quickly, asks questions, and turns feedback into better work. This role is equally technical and collaborative, and strong technical skills alone will not carry the work. Prior supply chain experience is preferred but not required. Curiosity about how a global supply chain works matters more, and you will learn the domain here.

You are someone who:

- Investigates the data instead of accepting it, and asks the question behind the question.
- Traces a number end to end - from the process that generated it, to the table it lands in, to the decision it drives.
- Partners with stakeholders instead of taking requirements at face value, and asks what decision the work needs to support.
- Is proactive and takes initiative.

ADDED ADVANTAGE

- Interest in supply chain, or a stated desire to build a career in supply chain and operations.
- A supply chain project taken end to end, from raw data through something someone actually used.
- Class or personal projects using LLM applications (RAG pipelines, agents, or evaluation harnesses).
- Public portfolio such as GitHub, Kaggle, or Tableau Public demonstrating applied projects.
